<reason>A wins by making the actual trade-off clearer: recurring access to important live games versus some additional exclusivity revenue, not access versus a funded league. A directly answered both pressure questions, acknowledged a possible net revenue sacrifice, and clarified that most marquee inventory remains monetizable. B raised a legitimate opportunity-cost objection but repeatedly exaggerated its consequences, misrepresented A’s concessions, and incorrectly insisted that free-to-air requires cable. B also failed to explain why additional revenue would reliably produce benefits outweighing the access A preserves.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A decisively challenged B’s purported substitutes for free live viewing: highlights, radio, and text do not provide the same experience, while cheaper passes still require payment. This exposed B’s failure to answer the central access question despite being pressed directly.</best_rebuttal>
